launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-tasks
description: Diego's Cloud Tasks (formerly Cloud Agenda, before that Cloud Calendar) — standalone Android task, calendar and event app. The applicationId stays com.diegonmarcos.cloudagenda so installed phones update in place. Jetpack Compose chrome (CloudKitTheme light/dark/system, libs:bottomnav island + page tabs, a page-managed hamburger drawer, AI and Profile buttons in the top row, libs:ai chat with persistent history) over a local tasks database (projects > lists > tasks > subtasks, statuses, tags, links to Cloud Mail / Cloud Drive items) and a mail agent that proposes tasks for review. The Events, Calendar and Invites pages are still the legacy tasks.html WebView (public-ICS feed sync, CalDAV against a self-hosted Radicale). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:databackend._doc_dir: #825 the engine wire (IDataBackend + DataBackendClient/Service), out of libs:core so a wire edit rebuilds only the engines and the apps that bind one.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:bottomnav._doc: #868 the fleet's bottom island (BottomNavIsland) and page-tab strip (PageTabs), and NavDecl, which reads ui.bottom_nav/ui.sections as baked into BuildConfig.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:nav-bar-bottom._doc: #1157 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:nav-bar-top-first-row._doc: #1157 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:nav-bar-top-second-row._doc: #1157 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1157 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ui-kit._doc: The Compose kit: CloudKitTheme and the palette roles every page paints with, the settings rows, chips, segmented picks and banners. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The AI dropdown: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only), sessions kept in the app's files dir so the history is permanent. Shared BY REFERENCE. This app holds no OpenRouter token and reads none (decisions-use guard D5): the gateway holds the fleet key. Its mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle. The mail agent's extraction calls the same gateway.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor (assets/agents/agents.json) its Agent picker and the Agent settings page list. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

engines._doc: ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING (engine-apk-split F2; same shape as ac_cloud-me/build.json::engines). `fleet` is the Store row in aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json from which app/build.gradle resolves the package (an unknown id fails the build) for BuildConfig and <queries> -- without the query Android 11+ hides the engine and CalBridge read it as not installed; `action` finds the service in it ({package} substituted at build time, matching the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT that answers every method CalBridge calls, read through PackageManager BEFORE binding. Cloud Me binds the same engine: one calendar cache, one task mirror.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

ui._doc: #868 THE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island's ids, ui.sections the section each one opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. Tasks is the native Compose page (hamburger drawer = projects and lists). Calendar is the legacy tasks.html WebView, one page per tab of the old shell (Events, Calendar, Invites). Settings is NOT on the island: it opens from the top bar's Settings > Configs, and its pages (Appearance, Agent, Inbox, Feeds) are the section's tab strip. Every section's `background` is `theme`: the strips follow the app's light / dark mode (Settings > Appearance), through NavDecl.stripSurface.

top_bar._doc: THE first row of the app (libs:bottomnav AppTopBar, declared once for the fleet): a hamburger that opens a side drawer the CURRENT page fills (the Tasks page: the projects and their lists; Calendar and Settings: their pages), the title, and two circular buttons: AI (libs:ai's chat in an anchored panel, one box for search and chat, history kept) and Settings (Account launches Cloud Account; Configs opens the Settings section: Appearance, Agent, Inbox, Feeds). No app draws its own copy of this row (cloud-android-top-bar-guard).

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. shell = the static testers under test/ (the declared navigation and its Kotlin ids; the screenshot parser). unit = gradle test: the data model, migrations, seeding, filter logic and the mail agent's parsing as JVM tests, and the Robolectric Compose layout-tree tests of the chrome (drawer, top row, filter bar, task editor).

shell._doc_requires: test-agents-parser.sh runs the screenshot parser under node; a missing tool must fail the preflight rather than draw a verdict from its own absence.

fleet_agents.name: Mail tasks agent
fleet_agents.trigger: periodic (Settings > Agent > frequency) or Run now
